# Sattrix Information Security Limited
## 1. Executive Verdict

**Pending evidence / research hold. BQS NS, GQS NS, IAS NS. Not a compounder designation or a new-purchase recommendation.** The issuer has a real cybersecurity delivery business and rising reported sales, but the investment question is whether additional software and acquisition capital produces durable external cash earnings per share. That is not established by the available primary evidence.

Three facts dominate. First, FY2026 consolidated sales reached ₹60.8344 crore and owner PAT ₹8.2360 crore, but the acquisition was a ₹157.8287513 crore related-party share swap with ₹130.6525 crore goodwill. Second, reported development capitalization and gross licence resale make EBITDA and growth less economically straightforward than a recurring software subscription business. Third, collections, earmarked investments and current funding need an updated bridge; incomplete BSE tape/lot evidence prevents an investability score. ([AR26](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/annual-report-25-26/25-26-Annual-Report.pdf), pp 175–204; [ALLOT](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/updates/2026/10-02-2026-revised-outcome-of-board-meeting.pdf), pp 3–7)

**Important resolved concern:** original 28 May 2026 audited results establish **positive FY2026 consolidated CFO ₹2.2269 crore**. The annual report’s three negative signs are a source-presentation discrepancy, not evidence of negative FY2026 operating cash. The original results also explicitly include the acquired subsidiary. Neither resolved matter is used to claim fraud, omitted consolidation or a qualified opinion. ([RESULTS](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/financials-information/2026/financial-results-for-2025-2026.pdf), PDF 18/21/23–24)

The positive counter-case is meaningful: legacy standalone revenue also grew 33.80%, original FY2026 financial/IFC opinions are unmodified, debt-service default was not identified, and March group mutual funds exceeded gross borrowings. Yet those facts do not establish unrestricted October cash, acquisition fairness, normalized software profit or executable exit liquidity. The conditional model deliberately distinguishes these unknowns from modeled shortfalls.

## 4. Business Overview

Founded 16 September 2013, Sattrix supplies cybersecurity licences/products, managed SOC/NOC and infrastructure services, professional services and consulting. Product risk/reward transfer and service time/milestone recognition are distinct. FY2026 products ₹38.4585 crore comprise licences ₹34.1492 crore and trading ₹4.3093 crore; services ₹22.3758 crore. Products are 63.22% of revenue, **licence-only 56.13%**. A gross licence sale is not subscription ARR, nor is licence procurement economically equivalent to a software developer’s gross margin. ([AR26](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/annual-report-25-26/25-26-Annual-Report.pdf), revenue note 20; [AR24](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/financials-information/annual-report-2023-24.pdf), policy/revenue notes pp 116–129)

The group includes US and UAE 100%-owned security subsidiaries, Malaysia 51% with 49% minority interest, and Sattrix Software Solutions Private Limited 100% acquired 10 February 2026. Malaysia control/investment date is 13 October 2025. UAE DMCC renamed FZCO 4 June 2026. The annual AOC-1/board list omits the new Indian target, but the original May auditor annexure and consolidation notes explicitly include it. This is a disclosure-list omission, not evidence the financial consolidation omitted the entity. ([RESULTS](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/financials-information/2026/financial-results-for-2025-2026.pdf), PDF 18/23–24; [AR26](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/annual-report-25-26/25-26-Annual-Report.pdf), AOC-1 and notes)

The acquired NewEvol platform may add proprietary economics, but pre-acquisition target FY2025 revenue ₹3.0168 crore was 98.62% to related parties, including ₹1.7348 crore to the listed acquirer. Those sales cannot all become incremental external group sales. The remaining target sales were only ₹0.0415 crore outside those two named related parties; this does not prove every other sale was unrelated. ([TARGET](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/group-company/sss-pvt/financial-statements-for-fy-2024-2025.pdf), PDF 26/32)

Customer names, contract duration, direct-versus-channel billings, renewal cohort economics, licence pass-through and the target’s post-acquisition external contribution are not sufficiently reconciled. They remain explicit limits, not assumed moat or assumed absence of customers.

## 5. Moat / Industry Position

There are plausible switching frictions in monitoring operations, integrations, security expertise and response processes. Conversely, vendor licences, skilled-labour competition, principal/customer concentration and a small independently proven proprietary-product base constrain demonstrated pricing power. Management’s July presentation claims 71% recurring revenue, >70% retention,60+active clients, nine clients over ₹1 crore and 10+relationships over three years. These definitions are not audited cohorts: retention could be logo rather than rupee retention, and licence renewals do not guarantee stable contribution margin. Hence MOAT is NS rather than a confident weak or strong score. ([PRESENTATION](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/investor-presentation/investor-presentation-2026.pdf), business/financial slides)

## 7. Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway

Actual renewal/new-work releases support DUR 6 with Medium confidence in a mixed runway, not a high TAM-based score. Claimed BFSI 58.3% and telecom 20.6% mix imply concentration if measured consistently; growth needs diversified clients, billable specialists, partner access and collection discipline. Claimed 95% utilization/98% billability are M assertions, not audited unit economics. ([PRESENTATION](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/investor-presentation/investor-presentation-2026.pdf); [NEW](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/updates/2026/press-release-as-on-11-06-2026-for-new-work-orders.pdf); [RENEW](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/updates/2026/press-release-as-on-11-06-2026-for-renewal-work-orders.pdf))

## 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path

**Permanent-impairment risk: High**, based on goodwill-heavy acquisition capital, long receivables, uncertain external product monetization and potentially dilutive funding needs. This categorical economic-risk assessment is not a prediction of actual default.

The strongest bear case is not merely a market de-rating. Related acquisition value may fail to convert to external customers; licence and professional-service growth may require long receivable financing; development payroll can consume cash before product monetization; customer concentration can compress renewal economics. Existing aged AR, the alleged-fraud advance and demand loans may recover less than book. Restricted or inaccessible investments, supplier payments and refinancing can force expensive dilution before earnings catch up. These mechanisms connect to cash, capital and per-share value rather than duplicating one red flag across every factor.

The conditional bear may fail early operating cash or sustainable terminal economics even with finite financing. The October-resource sensitivity uses ₹0.20 crore immediate cash and ₹12 crore debt as an explicit adverse resource assumption, not a reconstructed balance sheet or assertion those are actual October figures. MF no-access, faster supplier payment, slower AR, ₹8 crore write-off,15% development spending and 15% interest stresses are retained individually. sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.content_markdown:
**Pending evidence / research hold. BQS NS, GQS NS, IAS NS. Not a compounder designation or a new-purchase recommendation.** The issuer has a real cybersecurity delivery business and rising reported sales, but the investment question is whether additional software and acquisition capital produces durable external cash earnings per share. That is not established by the available primary evidence.

Three facts dominate. First, FY2026 consolidated sales reached ₹60.8344 crore and owner PAT ₹8.2360 crore, but the acquisition was a ₹157.8287513 crore related-party share swap with ₹130.6525 crore goodwill. Second, reported development capitalization and gross licence resale make EBITDA and growth less economically straightforward than a recurring software subscription business. Third, collections, earmarked investments and current funding need an updated bridge; incomplete BSE tape/lot evidence prevents an investability score. ([AR26](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/annual-report-25-26/25-26-Annual-Report.pdf), pp 175–204; [ALLOT](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/updates/2026/10-02-2026-revised-outcome-of-board-meeting.pdf), pp 3–7)

**Important resolved concern:** original 28 May 2026 audited results establish **positive FY2026 consolidated CFO ₹2.2269 crore**. The annual report’s three negative signs are a source-presentation discrepancy, not evidence of negative FY2026 operating cash. The original results also explicitly include the acquired subsidiary. Neither resolved matter is used to claim fraud, omitted consolidation or a qualified opinion. ([RESULTS](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/financials-information/2026/financial-results-for-2025-2026.pdf), PDF 18/21/23–24)

The positive counter-case is meaningful: legacy standalone revenue also grew 33.80%, original FY2026 financial/IFC opinions are unmodified, debt-service default was not identified, and March group mutual funds exceeded gross borrowings. Yet those facts do not establish unrestricted October cash, acquisition fairness, normalized software profit or executable exit liquidity. The conditional model deliberately distinguishes these unknowns from modeled shortfalls.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.content_markdown:
Founded 16 September 2013, Sattrix supplies cybersecurity licences/products, managed SOC/NOC and infrastructure services, professional services and consulting. Product risk/reward transfer and service time/milestone recognition are distinct. FY2026 products ₹38.4585 crore comprise licences ₹34.1492 crore and trading ₹4.3093 crore; services ₹22.3758 crore. Products are 63.22% of revenue, **licence-only 56.13%**. A gross licence sale is not subscription ARR, nor is licence procurement economically equivalent to a software developer’s gross margin. ([AR26](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/annual-report-25-26/25-26-Annual-Report.pdf), revenue note 20; [AR24](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/financials-information/annual-report-2023-24.pdf), policy/revenue notes pp 116–129)

The group includes US and UAE 100%-owned security subsidiaries, Malaysia 51% with 49% minority interest, and Sattrix Software Solutions Private Limited 100% acquired 10 February 2026. Malaysia control/investment date is 13 October 2025. UAE DMCC renamed FZCO 4 June 2026. The annual AOC-1/board list omits the new Indian target, but the original May auditor annexure and consolidation notes explicitly include it. This is a disclosure-list omission, not evidence the financial consolidation omitted the entity. ([RESULTS](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/financials-information/2026/financial-results-for-2025-2026.pdf), PDF 18/23–24; [AR26](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/annual-report-25-26/25-26-Annual-Report.pdf), AOC-1 and notes)

The acquired NewEvol platform may add proprietary economics, but pre-acquisition target FY2025 revenue ₹3.0168 crore was 98.62% to related parties, including ₹1.7348 crore to the listed acquirer. Those sales cannot all become incremental external group sales. The remaining target sales were only ₹0.0415 crore outside those two named related parties; this does not prove every other sale was unrelated. ([TARGET](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/group-company/sss-pvt/financial-statements-for-fy-2024-2025.pdf), PDF 26/32)

Customer names, contract duration, direct-versus-channel billings, renewal cohort economics, licence pass-through and the target’s post-acquisition external contribution are not sufficiently reconciled. They remain explicit limits, not assumed moat or assumed absence of customers.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.content_markdown:
There are plausible switching frictions in monitoring operations, integrations, security expertise and response processes. Conversely, vendor licences, skilled-labour competition, principal/customer concentration and a small independently proven proprietary-product base constrain demonstrated pricing power. Management’s July presentation claims 71% recurring revenue, >70% retention,60+active clients, nine clients over ₹1 crore and 10+relationships over three years. These definitions are not audited cohorts: retention could be logo rather than rupee retention, and licence renewals do not guarantee stable contribution margin. Hence MOAT is NS rather than a confident weak or strong score. Claimed BFSI 58.3% and telecom 20.6% mix imply concentration if measured consistently; growth needs diversified clients, billable specialists, partner access and collection discipline. sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.content_markdown:
**Audit history, not just the latest clean opinion.** FY2021 NMV & Associates issued an unmodified original standalone opinion; IFC reporting was exempt. FY2022–23 original CARO identified missing proper PPE/intangible records, related/demand loans without stipulated schedules and noncharging-interest exceptions. FY2022 foreign component revenue ₹1.3142 crore and FY2023 foreign revenue ₹2.7137 crore relied on management-certified/unaudited information. These were narrower assurance scopes, not all fully audited subsidiaries. ([AR21](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/financials-information/annual-report-for-fy-2020-2021.pdf), PDF 10–17; [AR22](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/financials-information/annual-report-for-fy-2021-2022.pdf), PDF 16–25/31–36; [AR23](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/financials-information/annual-report-for-fy2022-2023.pdf), PDF 29–46)

FY2023 unmodified opinions included emphasis on overseas investment compliance, a WDV-to-SLM depreciation change, ₹1.4202608 crore sales/marketing relationship-development capitalization and ₹1.1780946 crore unbilled/unearned service revenue. Later IPO special-purpose audit/restatement adjustments do not retroactively turn that original opinion into a qualified one. The prospectus says ODI regularization was pending at its own date, not proof it remains pending inOctober 2026. ([AR23](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/financials-information/annual-report-for-fy2022-2023.pdf); [PROSPECTUS](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/ipo/sattrix-prospectus.pdf), printed 175–181/207–208)

FY2024 G.K.Choksi & Co. and FY2025–26 A.N.Ruparel & Co. gave unmodified financial/IFC opinions. FY2024 proper asset records and IFC improvement are favorable subsequent evidence. FY2024 CARO notes auditor resignation but no issues from the outgoing auditor requiring consideration; FY2025 reports retirement without objections. Do not infer adverse resignation merely from firm change. ([AR24](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/financials-information/annual-report-2023-24.pdf), pp 69–78/106–111; [AR25](https://www.sattrix.com/annual-report-24-25/annual-report.pdf), pp 89–99/142–149; [AR26](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/annual-report-25-26/25-26-Annual-Report.pdf), pp 105–118/164–174)

FY2024 audit trail is described as operating without observed tampering. FY2025 and FY2026 consolidated language retains an unspecified exception phrase and no explicit statutory-preservation assurance; no separate FY2026 standalone trail paragraph was located. This is a disclosure/assurance limit, not proof logs were disabled or altered. ([AR25](https://www.sattrix.com/annual-report-24-25/annual-report.pdf), pp 93/146; [AR26](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/annual-report-25-26/25-26-Annual-Report.pdf), p 171)

**Current material matters.** The ₹1.4140 crore government-project vendor advance is a KAM concerning reported third-party fraud/forged authorizations, FIRCr 67/2025 and ongoing recovery. Management considers it recoverable, with no provision. It is not a qualified opinion, proven issuer misconduct or realized recovery. CARO explains no company officer/employee involvement for its ADT-4 treatment. The model assumes no recovery unless explicitly stressed. Continuing ₹0.1328 crore undisputed March 2023 GST arrears are an actual compliance finding, not a disputed-tax litigation estimate. ([AR26](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/annual-report-25-26/25-26-Annual-Report.pdf), pp 106/113–114/163/223; [AR24](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/financials-information/annual-report-2023-24.pdf)/[AR25](https://www.sattrix.com/annual-report-24-25/annual-report.pdf) CARO)

**Related-party acquisition and dilution.** The exact share swap issued 4,548,379 shares@₹347 for 12,001 target shares,379:1. Issued equity rose 66.89%; pre-existing shares represent 59.92% of the enlarged total before ownership overlap.₹130.6525 crore goodwill equals 82.78% of consideration. Historical target PAT ₹1.5063 crore and book equity ₹0.9914 crore imply 104.78× PAT and 159.20× book comparison ratios, but they are not acquisition-date values or a concluded fairness test. Independent valuation is asserted; the underlying valuation report, acquisition-date net assets/cash and post-acquisition contribution are not located. ([ALLOT](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/updates/2026/10-02-2026-revised-outcome-of-board-meeting.pdf); [TARGET](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/group-company/sss-pvt/financial-statements-for-fy-2024-2025.pdf); [AR26](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/annual-report-25-26/25-26-Annual-Report.pdf), goodwill note)

Source inconsistencies are carefully delimited: FY2026 CARO says no preferential placement despite the verified swap; capital note says no noncash allotments then describes the swap; an RPT row is ten times the correct investment amount; parent shares issued are mislabeled as target shares held. The exact allotment controls, not the erroneous row.13 January corrigendum reduced the earlier aggregate by ₹1,429 and changed relevant date to 30 October 2025; it supersedes an earlier corrigendum rather than adding consideration. ([AR26](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/annual-report-25-26/25-26-Annual-Report.pdf), pp 114/131/142/160/188; [CORRPREF](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/financials-information/2026/13-01-2026-Corrigendum-to-the-Notice-of-EGM.pdf))

Standalone FY2026 target advances ₹4.1682 crore, returns ₹1.6915 crore, purchases ₹1.1152 crore and asset purchase ₹3 crore require elimination and capital-transfer mapping. US subsidiary sales ₹4.8567 crore and receivable ₹4.9468 crore are not automatically external group sales. Target FY2025 related sales/purchase returns and ₹0.10 crore interest match the acquirer’s notes, favorable cross-source consistency. ([AR26](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/annual-report-25-26/25-26-Annual-Report.pdf), RPT notes; [AR25](https://www.sattrix.com/annual-report-24-25/annual-report.pdf), pp 138–139; [TARGET](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/group-company/sss-pvt/financial-statements-for-fy-2024-2025.pdf), PDF 32)

A current verified promoter-encumbrance and lock-in/free-float bridge is ND. The 25.04% March public holding is not automatically freely tradeable inventory; market-maker ownership, lock-ins, connected holders and lot constraints can reduce effective float. No later pledge or release is inferred from missing filings.

Directors’ remuneration ₹1.0575 crore is unchanged FY2025–26, approximately 12% ofFY2026 parent PAT. A separate ₹4.1453 crore Sachhin Gajjaer “reimbursement/loss in investment” category needs invoices/breakdown; it is not relabeled as salary, personal-loss reimbursement or a loan. Promoters hold 74.96% at 31 March 2026, with Ronak 55.50% and Sachhin 19.47%; Kedia Securities 8.06% is ownership, not third-party endorsement of value. ([AR26](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/annual-report-25-26/25-26-Annual-Report.pdf), RPT/capital notes; [SHP](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/shareholding-pattern/shareholding-pattern-31-03-2026.pdf))

**IPO/ESOP discipline.** Earlier in-house-to-outsourced development variation was shareholder-approved, not automatically unauthorized diversion. The later ₹3.3208 crore office/fixed-asset reallocation was board-proposed 26 August 2026 subject to shareholders; the notice alone proves neither passage nor completed purchase. Corrected ESOP pool ₹47.34862539 crore is a value cap, not a fixed option count;12 year vesting and valuer-set grant price replace four-year/₹[0] placeholders. Actual grants/approval implementation remain ND. Model reserve assumptions are not actual diluted shares. ([RESULTS](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/financials-information/2026/financial-results-for-2025-2026.pdf), PDF 24/27–29; [AR26](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/annual-report-25-26/25-26-Annual-Report.pdf), pp 27–28/45; [CORR](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/financials-information/corrigendum-to-notice-of-13th-annual-general-meeting-&-integrated-annual-report-2025-2026.pdf))

### Dated commitments and observable delivery

| Dated objective / claim | Verified milestone by cutoff | Economic delivery still to verify |
|---|---|---|
| IPO objective: in-house product/technology development; 16 January 2025 postal-ballot notice | Original May 2026 results confirm shareholder-approved change to outsourced development | Product-wise cash spent, commissioning and external customer returns, not merely asset additions |
| 10 February 2026 related-party acquisition | Share swap allotted and target consolidated from the disclosed acquisition date | Acquired external revenue/PAT/cash contribution and return on total consideration |

This is a table of observable milestones, not invented profit guidance or proof that every unverified item is a missed promise. Sources: ([RESULTS](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/financials-information/2026/financial-results-for-2025-2026.pdf); [ALLOT](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/updates/2026/10-02-2026-revised-outcome-of-board-meeting.pdf); [NEW](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/updates/2026/press-release-as-on-11-06-2026-for-new-work-orders.pdf); [RENEW](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/updates/2026/press-release-as-on-11-06-2026-for-renewal-work-orders.pdf); [AR26](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/annual-report-25-26/25-26-Annual-Report.pdf); [CORR](https://www.sattrix.com/images/investors/financials-information/corrigendum-to-notice-of-13th-annual-general-meeting-&-integrated-annual-report-2025-2026.pdf)).

### Explicit cash model

The nominal INR WACC range of 14–18% (16% base) is an analyst risk range, not a fitted CAPM estimate: small scale, concentrated clients, working-capital funding, uncertain development payback and minority-governance exposure warrant a high capital charge despite modest reported debt. It is separate from the 15% equity-return hurdle. Terminal g of 3–5% is kept below WACC and requires replacement software, fixed capital, working capital and operating cash. The model starts with **conditional March 31 balances carried to 19 October**, not an observed October balance or reconstructed pre-entry bridge. No-new-finance, uncommitted ₹4 crore bank and bounded ₹8 crore bank+₹10 crore equity are distinct regimes. The bank borrowing base is 75% of 90% AR with **zero FD collateral credit**. Equity begins only 19 January 2027 at 80% trialentry/floor ₹50,3% fees, whole shares and authorized-headroom limits. No-new debt repayment over 12 months is a callable/repayment stress, not established contractual maturity. Conditional annual 0.2224 crore amortization is an analyst policy. Daily/event cash gaps cannot be rescued by later annual receipts.

Every development rupee, fixed maintenance/growth investment, opening claim, tax, bank/equity fee and debt repayment is paid. Software 36 month and PPE 96 month straight-line cohorts affect EBIT/taxes; opening remaining lives are assumptions. Terminal steady software/fixed capital, future development, working capital and growing operating cash are paid for. sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.content_markdown:
**Permanent-impairment risk: High**, based on goodwill-heavy acquisition capital, long receivables, uncertain external product monetization and potentially dilutive funding needs. This categorical economic-risk assessment is not a prediction of actual default.

The strongest bear case is not merely a market de-rating. Related acquisition value may fail to convert to external customers; licence and professional-service growth may require long receivable financing; development payroll can consume cash before product monetization; customer concentration can compress renewal economics. Existing aged AR, the alleged-fraud advance and demand loans may recover less than book. Restricted or inaccessible investments, supplier payments and refinancing can force expensive dilution before earnings catch up. These mechanisms connect to cash, capital and per-share value rather than duplicating one red flag across every factor.

The conditional bear may fail early operating cash or sustainable terminal economics even with finite financing. The October-resource sensitivity uses ₹0.20 crore immediate cash and ₹12 crore debt as an explicit adverse resource assumption, not a reconstructed balance sheet or assertion those are actual October figures. MF no-access, faster supplier payment, slower AR, ₹8 crore write-off,15% development spending and 15% interest stresses are retained individually. Unverified current financing means G 3 Hold, not evidenced actual default.

Claims include operating/capital payables, statutory/salary/interest, debt, employee provision and DTL. This historical asset-recovery stress demonstrates limited tangible downside cover, not a liquidation recommendation or proof of insolvency.

**Thesis-break variables:** absent external acquired-product cash return after seasoning; recurring capitalization without realizable software economics; unreconciled acquisition/related-party transfers; sustained adverse collection/creditor stretch after current balances are obtained; or evidence of material minority abuse.
